notes:
THE 'Confirmed' TRAP IS PRESENT AND THE REGISTER SURVIVES IT: the Board rejected this claim outright on 19 Sept 1854 and the register's bare 'Confirmed' is true only because Judge Ogier reversed on 9 Feb 1858; the U.S. appeal to the Supreme Court was then dismissed for failure to docket and the DC declared its decree final on 1 Nov 1860. A reader who stopped at the Commission decree would have called this record wrong. Single volume; no second volume exists (the Wayback CDX for record/267550 lists only cubanc_lcf_sd206.pdf).

Alvarado added the partner by a second decree on the petition of 10 May 1837, stamped PAGE 16 (img22): 'Let this be added to the preceding and Cosme Vinegas be considered as included in the Decree of Concession of the 14th of last April.' The Deputation's grant names both, stamped PAGE 13 (img18): 'Se concede al Ciud.o Crisogono Ayala y á Cosme Bonegas, el paraje nombrado Sta Ana', translated stamped PAGE 18 (img24) 'There is granted to Citizen Crisogono Ayala and Cosme Banegas the place called Santa Ana'. No claimant-for-grantee substitution: the claimants ARE Ayala and the Venegas/Ayala heirs.

land_case.evidence: img1 red label 'CASE No. 97 SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; img2 typed slip 'LAND CASE 97 SD 123 pgs.'; every leaf stamped '97 SD PAGE n'; Bancroft filename cubanc_lcf_sd097.pdf. Board docket No. 494 (transcript title, stamped PAGE 1) = Hoffman's commission_no 494.

outcome.evidence: Confirmed at the Board and AFFIRMED on the United States' appeal, so no reversal trap here. Board opinion (Comm. Thompson Campbell) stamped PAGE 35 (img42): 'The petitioners are therefore entitled to a decree of confirmation as tenants in common of the place called "Santa Ana" which will be accordingly entered'; decree stamped PAGE 36 (img43) signed Felch, Campbell and R. Aug. Thompson, filed 24 Jan 1854 (stamped PAGE 37, img44). U.S. petition for review served 24 Aug 1855, stamped PAGE 122 (img132), which itself recites the claim was 'confirmed on the 24th day of Jany AD 1854'. Intervenor Camarillo's sworn petition, stamped PAGE 89 (img96): 'said last mentioned Grant was confirmed to the successors in interest of said Ayala and Vanegas, by said Board of Land Commissioners by its Decree of date January 24 1854, which Decree was approved by this Court on appeal, by its Decree entered in said Case No. 97, October 9th 1855, which last Decree was made final February 5, 1857.' Consistent with the court's own later orders: 20 Sept 1860 order restraining transmission of the approved survey (stamped PAGES 80-81, img89-90) and the 2 Dec 1862 order of Judge Fletcher M. Haight dismissing Camarillo's exceptions to the survey (stamped PAGE 113, img123).

notes:
Clean record on all six fields. TWO THINGS A RE-READER SHOULD KNOW.
(1) TRANSLATION-vs-ORIGINAL DATE CONFLICT, present here and NOT harmless to anyone reading the English alone. The Spanish expediente, stamped 97 SD PAGE 13 (img18), carries two distinct Deputation dates: the committee's proposition 'Sta Barbara. 16 de Mayo de 1837. José R. Estrada. Franc.o J. Alvarado', and the session that adopted it 'Sta Barbara. Mayo de 18 de 1837. En Sesion de hoy se le dispensaron los tramites á la proposicion del dictamen que antecede y fué aprobado por mejoria absoluta.' The sworn English translation, stamped PAGES 18-19 (img24-25), renders BOTH as 'May 16th 1837' and drops the dispensing-with-formalities clause. The Board itself went by the Spanish: its opinion, stamped PAGE 34 (img41), says 'on the 18th day of May 1837 the said grant was duly confirmed by the Departmental Assembly', as does the claim petition (stamped PAGE 4, img9). None of this touches a register field (the register carries only the grant year), but any downstream date of Deputation approval should be taken as 18 May 1837 from the Spanish, not 16 May from the translation.
(2) THE GRANT IS TWO DECREES, NOT ONE, and the register's two-name grantee is only correct because of the second. Ayala petitioned alone on 10 Feb 1837 and was made sole owner on 14 Apr 1837; he then petitioned to associate Cosme Venegas and Alvarado ordered on 10 May 1837 that Venegas 'be considered as included in the Decree of Concession of the 14th of last April'. The Deputation's approval names both. A register that carried only 'Crisogono Ayala' (as Hoffman's 'Crisogono Ayala et al.' effectively does) would be defensible on the 14 April decree alone; the register's fuller reading is the better one.

SPELLING: the file spells the second grantee Venegas / Vanegas / Banegas / Bonegas interchangeably, sometimes twice on one leaf. The register's 'Vanegas' is one of the file's own forms; not an error.

year.evidence: Spanish concession decree, stamped 368 SD PAGE 19 (img22): 'Santa Barbara Julio 4 de 1846. Vista la anterior solicitud ... he venido por las presentes letras en declarar al señor Don Tomas Robbins, dueño en propiedad de la Isla de Santa Catalina...'. Titulo, stamped PAGE 23 (img26), 'Dado en el puerto de Santa Barbara ... á los cuatro dias del mes de julio del año mil ochocientos cuarenta y seis'. Sworn translations agree, stamped PAGES 22 and 25 (img25, img28). Restated as a finding of the District Court decree, stamped PAGE 47 (img53): 'being the same granted to Thomas Robbins by Governor Pio Pico on the fourth day of July 1846'.

The decree declares 'al señor Don Tomas Robbins, dueño en propiedad' (stamped PAGE 19, img22); the petition is signed 'Santa Barbara Julio 4 de 1846 ... Robbins' (stamped PAGE 18, img21). The U.S.-era claimant was Jose Maria Covarrubias, who bought the island from Robbins for $10,000 by deed of 31 Aug 1850 (stamped PAGE 29, img32) and is the man on the red label, in the case title, and in the register's patent_to field. land_case.evidence: img1 red label 'CASE No. 368 SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; img2 typed slip 'LAND CASE 368 SD pgs. 58'; every leaf stamped '368 SD PAGE n'; District Court wrapper 'No. 368' (img40); Bancroft filename cubanc_lcf_sd368.pdf. Board docket No. 547 (transcript title, stamped PAGE 1) = Hoffman's commission_no 547.

outcome.evidence: Confirmed, affirmed on appeal, and the appeal to the Supreme Court abandoned by the United States - the whole chain is in this one volume. Board decree No. 547, stamped PAGE 32 (img36): 'it is adjudged by the Commission that the claim of the said Petitioner is valid and it is therefore decreed that the same be confirmed to him ... known as the Island of Santa Catalina, and is bounded on all sides by the Sea', Felch / R. Aug. Thompson / S.B. Farwell, filed 25 Sept 1855. Attorney General Caleb Cushing's notice of appeal, stamped PAGE 35 (img41), 11 Feb 1856. District Court, December Term 1857, stamped PAGES 47-48 (img53-54): 'the decision of said Board of Land Commissioners confirming unto the above named appellee Jose Maria Covarrubias ... be and the same is hereby affirmed, And that the title of the said Covarrubias to the said land is a good and valid one ... to the extent of eleven square leagues, and no more, and has for its boundaries the waters edge', Isaac S.K. Ogier, U.S. Dist. Judge; filed 1 March 1858 (stamped PAGE 49, img55). Supreme Court No. 305, Dec. Term 1864: Attorney General James Speed's discontinuance, stamped PAGE 56 (img62), Washington 29 March 1865, 'being satisfied that there is no just ground for prosecuting this appeal, I do hereby discontinue the further prosecution thereof ... and that the claimant be at liberty to proceed and obtain a survey and patent in conformity with the decree of confirmation'; dismissal entered and certified by Clerk D.W. Middleton the same day (stamped PAGE 57, img63); mandate filed in the District Court 15 Aug 1865 (stamped PAGE 58, img64).

notes:
CLEAN, AND IT IS THE CONTROL CASE FOR THIS AUDIT'S DOMINANT ERROR CLASS. Every condition for the claimant-for-grantee substitution is present - the grantee (Thomas M. Robbins) sold out in 1850, the claimant (Jose Maria Covarrubias) is the name on the red label, on every wrapper, in the case caption, and in the register's own patent_to field - and the register still carries Robbins in the grantee slot. Whoever compiled this row read past the label to the grant.
DECREE CARRIES AN IMPOSSIBLE LATITUDE, and it is worth knowing before anyone 'corrects' a transcription. Robbins's petition of 4 July 1846 places the island 'á los 43 g.o 20 m.o de latitud Norte' and then adds an Otro si in his own hand (stamped PAGE 18, img21): 'la Isla que pretende esta situada á los 34 g.o 40 m. de latitud Norte á los 43 g.o que espresa mi instancia'. Pico's decree and the titulo both nevertheless repeat the erroneous 43 degrees, and the sworn English translations faithfully repeat it again (stamped PAGES 21-22 and 25). The island is of course at 33 degrees 20 minutes. This is an error IN the grant, not in anyone's transcription of it, and it never affected the case.
PRIOR REFUSED APPLICATION, useful context and a dating trap: Robbins first asked for the island from Monterey on 11 Feb 1839 (Exhibit P.L., Spanish stamped PAGE 27, translation stamped PAGE 28, img30-31), and John Forster testified he and James Johnson were refused the same island by Governor Alvarado 'about the year 1839 or 1840' (stamped PAGE 6, img9). Neither is the grant. A reader working from testimony rather than the decree could easily land on 1839 and Alvarado; the register's 1846 / Pio Pico is right.
STAMP/IMAGE DRIFT, small but not constant - cite stamped pages: img3=stamped 1 (drift 2), img22=stamped 19 (3), img36=stamped 32 (4), img41=stamped 35 (6), img53=stamped 47 (6), img64=stamped 58 (6). A third foliation, the clerk's transcript leaf number, runs in the top-left corner one behind the stamp, and the transcript's 'Vide page N' cross-references use that series.
PATENT (Phase C): no patent copy in the file; it ends with the Supreme Court mandate of Aug 1865. The register's patent to Jose M. Covarrubias, 10 Apr 1867, GLO 470, 45,820.43 acres is consistent with (and unblocked by) Speed's 1865 discontinuance, which expressly left the claimant free to obtain survey and patent, but is not itself verified here. Note the District Court capped the confirmation at eleven square leagues (about 48,700 acres), so the patent acreage sits inside the decree.

outcome.evidence: Confirmed at the Board, AFFIRMED on the United States' appeal, and the further appeal expressly abandoned. Board confirmed 24 Jan 1854, recited in the U.S. summons served on Sanchez, stamped 90 SD PAGE 33 (img41): 'the decision of final Confirmation of the Board of U.S. Land Commissioners ... to the Claim of Juan Sanchez for a tract of land called Santa Clara or El Norte in the County of Santa Barbara Cal. and presented by you to said Commissioners on or about the 9th day of October A.D. 1852 and by them Confirmed on the 24th day of January A.D. 1854'; Secretary George Fisher's certificate of the 34-page transcript, stamped PAGE 30 (img37), 12 Sept 1854. Attorney General Caleb Cushing's notice of appeal, stamped PAGE 31 (img39), 30 Nov 1854. DISTRICT COURT, December Term A.D. 1856, stamped PAGES 50-52 (img58-60): 'It is Ordered, adjudged and decreed by the Court that the decision of the said Commissioners be and the same is hereby affirmed, and that the title of the said appellee Juan Sanchez to the lands claimed in this case be decreed to be good and valid ... Provided that if the lands hereby confirmed and above described are of the extent of more than eleven square leagues, then confirmation is hereby made of eleven square leagues and no more', Isaac S.K. Ogier, U.S. Dist. Judge; filed 19 Jan 1857 (stamped PAGE 53, img61). Cushing again, Attorney General's Office 26 Jan 1857, stamped PAGE 54 (img62): 'In the case of the claim of Juan Sanchez, confirmed to the claimant by the Commissioners, case no. three hundred and eighty-nine (389), appeal will not be prosecuted by the United States'; filed 4 March 1858 (stamped PAGE 55, img63), the last leaf of the file.

notes:
Clean on all six fields, and unusually well evidenced: the grant date, the governor and the grantee are each stated twice, once in the Spanish decree and once independently in Judge Ogier's District Court decree, which is not copying the claim petition but making its own finding.
WHAT THE UNITED STATES ACTUALLY ATTACKED, worth recording because it shows the register's fields were never the contested ones: the U.S. exceptions (stamped PAGES 43-46, img51-54) go entirely to FORM and PERFORMANCE, not to the grant's date, author or beneficiary - that the espediente is on unstamped paper, that Joaquin Carrillo's act of juridical possession of 29 July 1842 is unsigned by the two assisting witnesses and 'vague and indefinite', that there is no evidence Carrillo had authority to give possession, and that Sanchez did not prove he built and inhabited a house within a year. Ogier rejected all of it.
DATE I COULD NOT SETTLE, flagged rather than asserted: the Ayuntamiento committee's report on the espediente (stamped PAGE 9, img14) carries a May 1837 date I could not read with confidence at this resolution; it must fall between Alvarado's referral of 25 April and his concession of 6 May, so my tentative reading of the numeral is wrong somewhere. Nothing in the register depends on it. The two dates that matter, 6 May 1837 (concession) and 20 May 1837 (Deputation), are both legible and both corroborated - by the claim petition (stamped PAGE 4, img9) and, for the first, by the District Court.
NO ENGLISH TRANSLATION OF THE EXPEDIENTE IN THE LEAVES I READ: the file gives the Spanish original certified by Surveyor General Samuel D. King, 29 June 1853, as 'the eight preceding ... pages numbered from one to eight' (stamped PAGES 10-11, img15-16). All my year/governor/grantee grades rest on the Spanish itself, so the translation-vs-original trap cannot bite here.
THREE FOLIATIONS, and in this file they are NOT in the usual order - cite the stamped page. The Bancroft stamp runs BEHIND the clerk's own transcript foliation at the end: Fisher's certificate calls the transcript 'thirty four pages, numbered from 1 to 34' but sits on stamped PAGE 30 (img37), and the leaf carrying clerk number 34 is img36. The transcript's internal 'Vide page N' references use the clerk's series, so the Board opinion cited as 'page 31' is NOT stamped PAGE 31 (which is Cushing's appeal notice). Image-to-stamp drift: img5=stamped 1 (4), img13=stamped 8 (5), img37=stamped 30 (7), img41=stamped 33 (8), img63=stamped 55 (8).
NOT READ: the Board's own opinion and decree leaves (roughly stamped 27-29). The Board's confirmation is nevertheless established from three other documents in the file, quoted above. If a re-reader wants the Commissioners' reasoning verbatim it is in that stretch.
PATENT (Phase C): no patent copy in the file. Register's patent to Juan Sanchez, 5 Nov 1869, GLO 402, 13,988.91 acres is untested here; it sits well inside the decree's eleven-league cap.

name.evidence: Spanish expediente heading, stamped 406 ND PAGE 9 (img15): 'Espediente promovido p.r el Ciud.o Anastasio Chaboya, en solicitud del paraje nombrado Sanjon de los Moquelemes y p.r otro nombrado Las Calaveras. 1844.' Sworn translation, stamped PAGE 15 (img21): 'the tract of Land called Sanjon de los Moquelemnes and by another name Las Calaveras'. Board Secretary's certificate, stamped PAGE 32 (img39): 'for the place known by the name of Sanjon de los Muquelemes'. Red label (img1): 'SANJON de los MIQUELEMES GRANT'. Register's 'Moquelumnes' is Hoffman's printed form and an orthographic variant of the same river name; the file itself spells it four different ways.

year.evidence: Spanish concession decree, stamped 406 ND PAGE 12 (img18): 'Monterrey. 24 de En.o de 1844. Vista la peticion con que da principio este Espediente, los informes que preceden con todo lo demas que se tuvo presente y ser convino, de conformidad con las leyes y reglamentos de la materia declaro á D.n Anastasio Chabolla dueño de la estension de ocho sitios de ganado mayor...'. Marginal order the same day: 'Monterrey. En.o 24 de 1844. Espidase el titulo con ocho sitios atendiendo a ser siete hijos y ser hijo al pais y ciudadano Mejicano. Michelterena.' The titulo closes 'Dado en Monterrey á veinte cuatro de Enero de mil ochocientos cuarenta y cuatro' (stamped PAGE 20, img26). Restated as the District Court's own finding, stamped PAGE 68 (img76): 'being the same land described in the Decree of Concession dated January 24th 1844 and grant of the same date'.

governor.evidence: Titulo, Spanish, stamped 406 ND PAGE 19 (img25): 'Manuel Michelterena General de Brigada del Ejercito Mejicano, Ayudante General de la Plana Mayor del mismo, Gobernador Comand.te General é Inspector del Departamento de las Calif.as ... usando de las facultades que me son conferidas a nombre de la Nacion Mejicana hé benido en concederle el terreno mencionado'; signed 'Man.l Michelterena / Manuel Jimeno, Srio' (stamped PAGE 20, img26). Sworn translation stamped PAGES 21-22 (img27-28). Corroborated by Ignacio del Valle's deposition of 16 Oct 1852, stamped PAGE 6 (img12): 'What offices in California, if any, did the said persons hold on the 24 January 1844? Answer. Manuel Micheltorena was governor, & Manuel Jimeno Secretary.'

grantee.evidence: Concession decree, stamped 406 ND PAGE 12 (img18): 'declaro á D.n Anastasio Chabolla dueño de la estension de ocho sitios de ganado mayor'; sworn translation, stamped PAGE 18 (img24): 'I declare Anastasio Chabolla Owner of the Extent of Eight leagues for large cattle (ocho sitios de ganado mayor)'. Petition signed 'Pueblo de San José, Mayo 17 de 1843. Anastasio Chabolla' (stamped PAGE 11, img17). Claimant and grantee are the same man; on his death the claim was revived in the names of his seven children (order of Judge Ogden Hoffman, 24 March 1856, stamped PAGE 64, img72). Register 'A. Chabolla' = Anastasio Chabolla, and it uses the family's own Spanish spelling rather than the U.S. clerks' 'Chaboya' on the red label.

land_case.evidence: img1 red label 'CASE No. 406 NORTHERN DISTRICT'; img2 typed slip 'LAND CASE 406 ND 596 pgs.'; every leaf stamped '406 ND PAGE n'; District Court wrapper (img40) 'No. 406 ... Transcript of the Record from the Board of U.S. Land Commissioners, In Case No. 393, Filed February 6 1856'; Judge Hoffman's own caption, stamped PAGE 70 (img78), 'D.C. 406 : L.C. 393'. Bancroft filename cubanc_lcf_nd406.pdf; the digicoll OAI record for 264253 lists this one file only, so the case is a SINGLE volume despite the size. Board docket 393 = Hoffman's commission_no 393.

outcome.evidence: Confirmed, but ONLY on reversal, and the Board rejected TWICE. Transcript index, stamped 406 ND PAGE 3 (img8): 'San Francisco January 31 1854. In the same case Commissioner Thompson Campbell delivered the opinion of the Board rejecting the claim'; then 'San Francisco February 13, 1855 ... Ordered that the decree of rejection entered heretofore to wit on the 31st of January 1854 be set aside and the case be referred to and placed at the foot of the trial docket'; then 'San Francisco Sept 4th 1855. In the same case Commissioner S.B. Farwell delivered the opinion of the Board rejecting the claim.' DISTRICT COURT DECREE, stamped PAGES 66-68 (img74-76): 'it appearing to the Court that there is error in the said decision of the Board of Commissioners, it is by the Court hereby Ordered, adjudged and decreed that the said decision be and the same is reversed and in all things annulled. And the Court now proceeding to render such decision and judgment as should have been rendered herein, it is ordered, adjudged and decreed that the claim of the said Angel Maria Chabolla, José Antonio Chabolla, José Fernando Chabolla, José Facundo Chabolla, Maria Ygnacia Chabolla, Maria Juana Chabolla and Maria Micaela Policarpia Chabolla, only children and heirs of Anastasio Chabolla and Maria Josefa Higuera de Chabolla, his wife, both deceased, is a good and valid claim and that the said claim be and the same is hereby confirmed to the extent and quantity of Eight square leagues on the borders of the river Cosumnes Southward and on that of the San Joaquin, measuring Two leagues on the borders of the river San Joaquin and the rest on the plain to the East', signed Ogden Hoffman, U.S. Dist. Judge; filed 10 May 1856 (stamped PAGE 69, img77). U.S. appeal granted 29 July 1857 (stamped PAGE 70, img78). Supreme Court mandate DISMISSING the United States' appeal presented and ordered filed 17 Aug 1858, stamped PAGE 72 (img80): 'and that the said claimants may proceed under the decree of this Court heretofore rendered in favor of the claim of said claimants as under final decree', Ogden Hoffman.

notes:
SECOND INSTANCE IN THIS CHUNK OF THE 'Confirmed' TRAP, and the worse of the two: here the Land Commission rejected the claim TWICE, on 31 Jan 1854 and again on 4 Sept 1855 after its own first decree was set aside, and Anastasio Chabolla died before the second rejection. The register's bare 'Confirmed' is true only because Judge Ogden Hoffman reversed and annulled the Board's decision on 10 May 1856 and confirmed to the seven Chabolla children, and because the Supreme Court then dismissed the United States' appeal (mandate filed 17 Aug 1858). Anyone auditing this row against the Commission alone would score it wrong.
SPANISH ORIGINAL vs SWORN TRANSLATION, ON THE GRANTEE'S FORENAME - FLAGGED, NOT ASSERTED. The concession decree (stamped PAGE 12) and the sworn English translation of the titulo (stamped PAGE 21, 'the citizen Anastasio Chabolla') both read Anastasio. My reading of the SPANISH titulo itself, stamped 406 ND PAGE 19 (img25), is 'Por cuanto el Ciudadano ANTONIO Chabolla há pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia la estension de ocho sitios de ganado mayor'. If that reading is right the title deed misnames its own grantee and the translation silently corrects it - and the confusion is live, because Anastasio's brother ANTONIO Chabolla is a witness in this very file (deposition, stamped PAGE 46, img54: 'My name is Antonio Chabolla ... I knew Anistacio Chabolla he was my Brother'). I could not resolve the word to certainty at this resolution and am NOT reporting it as a finding. A re-reader should check that one line. Nothing turns on it for the register: the decree, the translation, the claim, and Hoffman's decree all say Anastasio.
*** BIGGEST TRAP IN THIS FILE FOR A LATER READER: A SECOND MICHELTORENA GRANT IS BOUND INSIDE IT. *** Stamped PAGES 49-61 (img57-69) are Exhibit M, the complete expediente of WILLIAM E. P. HARTNELL - petition Monterey 2 Nov 1844, titulo for ELEVEN leagues 'Dado en Monterrey este dia tres de Noviembre de mil ochocientos cuarenta y cuatro', certified by Surveyor General John C. Hays 27 Feb 1856, with the Departmental Assembly's action of 16 March 1846 signed by PIO PICO as President. It was put in evidence only because Hartnell's tract is bounded 'por el poniente con el rancho del Señor Anastacio Chaboya', i.e. to prove where Chabolla's rancho was. A reader skimming for 'the grant' in this 596-page file can very easily land on 3 Nov 1844 / Hartnell, or on Pio Pico's 1846 signature, and mis-grade year, governor and grantee all at once. The grant in suit is at stamped PAGES 12-13 and 19-22.
CATALOGUE vs FILE ON THE FIRST REJECTION DATE: the Bancroft/Bowman note on digicoll record/264253 says 'Rejected by the Board Jan. 24, 1854 and Sept. 4, 1855'. The transcript itself gives the first rejection as 31 January 1854, twice (the index entry and the order setting it aside, both stamped PAGE 3). 24 January 1854 looks like Bowman importing the grant's day-of-month. The second rejection date, 4 Sept 1855, agrees.
NOT READ, and named rather than guessed: Bowman also records a SECOND District Court confirmation on 5 Aug 1863. That decree lies beyond stamped PAGE 74 in the same single volume and I did not reach it; the file runs to 596 stamped pages / 604 images and the intervening 500 pages are survey and re-survey litigation. My 'Confirmed' grade rests on the 1856 decree, which Hoffman himself declared final in 1858, not on the 1863 one.
STAMP/IMAGE DRIFT: img5=stamped 1 (drift 4), img18=stamped 12 (6), img26=stamped 20 (6), img39=stamped 32 (7), img41=stamped 33 (8), img74=stamped 66 (8), img82=stamped 74 (8). A THIRD foliation, the clerk's transcript leaf number, runs in the top-left corner one behind the stamp, and the transcript's 'Vide page N' references use that series (the Sept 1855 rejection cited as 'page 29' is stamped PAGE 30). The exhibits carry a FOURTH numbering, their own Surveyor-General tracing-page numbers 1-8, restarting inside each exhibit.
PATENT (Phase C): no patent copy in the pages read. Register's patent to the heirs of Anastasio Chabolla, 30 May 1865, GLO 93, 35,508.14 acres is untested here, though it is consistent with the decree's eight square leagues (about 35,500 acres) - an unusually exact match, which is itself a small check on the register's acreage.

*** REGISTER-LEVEL FINDING, STATED AS A FINDING BUT DELIBERATELY NOT GRADED (no leaf read). The name on this row looks wrong, and wrong in a way that makes the row collide with another row in the same register. ***
The register has TWO Chino rows (data/ranchos-register.csv):
  rancho-santa-ana-chino | 'Santa Ana Del Chino (Addition To)' | 1841 | Alvarado | Antonio Maria Lugo | SD 182 | 22,234.20 acres | patent 15 Feb 1869 | GLO 478
  u-4                    | 'addition to Santa Ana del Chino'  | 1843 | Micheltorena | I. Williams | SD 335 | patent 29 Apr 1869 | GLO 478
The Bancroft catalogue (OAI-PMH marcxml, which is NOT WAF-challenged, so this evidence was obtainable today) separates them cleanly:
  record/267530, 024 'BANC MSS Land Case Files 182 SD', title 'Santa Ana del Chino [San Bernardino County] Isaac Williams, Claimant. Case no. 182, Southern District of California', 520 (from Bowman I, 758): 'Granted by Alvarado Mar. 26, 1841, to Antonio Maria Lugo; 5 leagues, by name. Claim filed by Isaac Williams Nov. 1, 1852. Confirmed by the Board Apl. 25, 1854. Confirmed by the District Court Jan. 13, 1857, and June 6, 1863. Patent issued to Maria Merced Williams and Francisca Williams de Carlisle Feb. 15, 1869, for 22,234.20 acres ... No. 477 General Land Office map. This grant was also called Chino.'
  record/268958, 024 '335 SD', 520 (Bowman I, 759): 'Granted by Micheltorena Mar. 22, 1843, to Julian Williams; 3 leagues, by description ... Confirmed by the Board May 8, 1855. Confirmed by the District Court Jan. 14, 1857, and June 9, 1863. Patent issued to Maria Merced Williams and Francisca Williams de Carlisle Apl. 29, 1869 for 13,366.16 acres ... No. 478 General Land Office map.'
So SD 182 is the CHINO ITSELF and SD 335 is the ADDITION. Every substantive value on the rancho-santa-ana-chino row (1841, Alvarado, Lugo, 22,234.20 acres, 15 Feb 1869) is the Chino's, and the register already carries the Addition separately at u-4. The words '(Addition To)' on this row therefore appear to be an intrusion, and they make the register look as though it has two Addition rows and no Chino row. RECOMMENDED (to be confirmed against the red label on the re-read): name should read 'Santa Ana del Chino'. Hoffman's 1862 table agrees - his row for court_no 182 reads plainly 'Santa Ana del Chino' - which is why hoffman_flags is empty even though the register's name string differs: the flagger evidently compared the two loosely.
SECOND, SMALLER ITEM FOR PHASE C: the register puts GLO 478 on BOTH Chino rows. Bowman gives 477 for the Chino (record/267530) and 478 for the Addition (record/268958), so 478 looks propagated from the Addition onto the Chino. Note the same propagation has already happened INSIDE the Bancroft catalogue: the 'Associated Case Numbers' line on record/267530 reads 'Toma 164, Expediente 522, Docket 434, 335 SD, GLO 478' - identical, character for character, to the line on record/268958, i.e. the Chino record carries the ADDITION's toma, expediente, docket, case number and GLO number. If the register was built partly from that catalogue, one contaminated field could explain both the '(Addition To)' and the 478. This is a hypothesis about provenance, not a finding.
